findings.title: Same NPE remains in the other paged/search subgroup methods
findings.body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). The three paged variants, getSubGroupsStream(search, firstResult, maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(firstResult, maxResults) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(search, exact, firstResult, maxResults) (line 268), still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without a null check. If the group was deleted concurrently, modelSupplier.get() returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR claims to fix. They need the same null handling, or should delegate through a path that throws a consistent error.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount silently returns null for a deleted group
findings.body: The new code returns null when the backing model is gone. GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount pass this straight to setSubGroupCount, and any caller that unboxes the Long will NPE. Returning null here moves the NPE to a different place rather than defining a clear contract (e.g. returning 0, or throwing a not-found-style exception consistently with the other methods that throw 'Not found in database').

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so late failures are silently ignored
findings.body: The background reader thread is started and the test asserts on caughtExceptions immediately after setting deletedAll=true, without joining the thread. A read that is in flight when the flag flips, and which fails afterwards, will add to the list after the assertion has already run, so the test passes while hiding the exception. The thread should be joined (with a timeout) before asserting. Also, the test never verifies that the deletions succeeded or that the groups are gone, and it leaves the 100 created groups without cleanup via managedRealm.cleanup().

findings.title: Unbounded busy-loop of HTTP admin calls in a non-daemon thread
findings.body: The reader loops with no sleep, issuing admin REST calls as fast as possible until the flag is set. If the main thread fails before setting deletedAll (for example, the fail() in the creation loop or a remove() exception), the flag is never set and this non-daemon thread spins forever, which can hang the test JVM. Wrapping the set in a finally block and making the thread a daemon or joining it would avoid this.
